thread:
sam: Heads-up — since the 03:00 deploy p50/p95 for rtb-serving on eu-west jumped ~2x. Noticed more kernel fallbacks and batch skew. Anyone else seeing this?
ops-bot: ALERT: latency_spike service=rtb-serving region=eu-west trigger=cpu-threshold (1794207850) <https://incidents.redwood/1794207850|details> :rotating_light:
jess: Yup, I saw the alert. Quick grep on profiler traces shows a pattern: heavy fallback to the slow attention kernel for sequences >1024.
kai: Interesting — did model variant change? Kernel selector rule should pick fused-attn for long seqs but looks like it's choosing generic fallback.
maria: KV cache pressure is high for several tenants, eviction rate spiked from 0.8% -> 9% in the last 10m. That could increase effective seq length (more cache misses).
sam: Good point. Maria can you list top offending tenants?
maria: Top offenders: tenant-831 (bulk streaming evals), tenant-194 (long-chained chat replays). tenant-831 has many concurrent streaming requests with small tokens per frame — causes lots of small batches.
leo: I pulled a flamegraph from the hotpath on the node handling tenant-831: show huge time in slow_gemm and freq of kernel_switch calls. Suspect batching heuristics produce many tiny batches and then violent cache churn.
jess: Uploading quick perf snippet: ```
# perf summary
p50 before: 62ms -> now: 138ms
p95 before: 180ms -> now: 420ms
kv_evictions_per_min: 0.8 -> 9.4
kernel_fallback_rate: 2% -> 23%
```
kai: Thanks. Two quick mitigation ideas: (1) temporary tenant-level concurrency throttle for tenant-831, (2) flip feature flag to stricter batching heuristic (batch_min_tokens=32, prefer-filled-batches=true).
sam: +1 on both. Ops: can we apply throttle ASAP and toggle flag in staging then prod?
ops-bot: RUNBOOK: To apply tenant throttling use: ```/throttle tenant tenant-831 qps=5 reason="incident-1794207890"```
leo: I ran a dry throttle in staging, it limited concurrency and improved batch sizes — p95 dropped ~30% in staging.
maria: I'm ready to apply throttle in prod for tenant-831. Will monitor cache evictions and kernel_fallback_rate.
jess: I'll prepare the flag patch and a short rollout plan with a 5-minute canary. Patch: ```yaml
feature_flags:
  batching_strict:
    default: false
    rollout: manual
    params:
      batch_min_tokens: 32
      prefer_filled_batches: true
```
kai: If we flip batching_strict=true, runtime will avoid creating tiny batches and prefer waiting up to 15ms for fill. That may slightly increase average latency for very low-volume requests but should cut kernel fallbacks.
sam: Do it. Prioritize tenant throttle first then flag canary. Also add a routing fallback: route tenant-831 to a dedicated node pool with larger KV cache if throttling not enough.
leo: I'll reserve a small pool (2 nodes) and create routing rule: ```
route:
  tenant: tenant-831
  pool: kv-large-pool
  weight: 1.0
```
ops-bot: CHANGE: tenant throttle tenant-831 qps=5 applied (1794208022) :white_check_mark:
maria: Immediately after throttle applied, eviction rate dropped to 4.1% and kernel_fallback_rate to 12%. p95 trending down.
jess: Batching flag canary deployed to 1% traffic (1794208120). Observing: batch sizes up from 6 -> 28 avg for this tenant. p95 reduced further.
sam: Great. What's the risk vector? Any degradation elsewhere?
kai: Risk is tail for tiny, latency-sensitive requests from other tenants. We'll scope canary to tenant-831 first then expand. Also added automatic rollback if cluster-wide p95 increases >10% in 5m.
leo: After routing tenant to kv-large-pool, node-level memory went up but evictions stabilized. No OOMs.
Maria: Telemetry after full throttle+flag+route: p50=68ms p95=165ms (back near baseline), kv_evictions=1.2, kernel_fallback_rate=4.5%.
sam: Excellent work. Next steps: 1) keep throttle for 2h and then evaluate soft-QoS instead of hard throttle, 2) bake batching_strict as opt-in for long sequences, 3) investigate kernel-selector bug for long seq detection. Assign: Kai on selector bug, Jess on flag rollout plan, Maria on eviction metrics, Leo on routing cleanup.
ops-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: latency_spike service=rtb-serving region=eu-west resolved (1794208655) :tada:
sam: Thanks team — please add a short incident note in postmortems with root cause and the mitigation timeline.
leo: I'll add flamegraphs and a small repro for noisy tenant behavior to the incident doc.
jess: I'll open a PR for batching_strict gradual rollout and a monitoring dashboard for kernel_fallback_rate.
kai: I'll add a unit test around sequence length classification and a check in the selector to avoid false positives.
maria: I'll keep an eye for recurrence and consider eviction-aware routing heuristics.
sam: Closing thread for now, will reopen if alerts reappear. :thumbsup:
